rules.scoring: Gains are rest-of-season points (rules.unit), worked in integers: h(x) = round(100*x) of a ros_pg or lineup.ros_floor value as the file carries it (2 decimals), t(x) = round(10*x) of a games value (1 decimal), W = the league's weeks_left. Candidates: every player of the roster, ir true or false, ordered by h(ros_pg) descending, then t(games) descending, then name ascending; each starts with left = t(games). Slot kinds, in order: each position P of lineup.slots (its n, pos list [P]), then each entry of lineup.flex in order (its n and pos list). For each kind: need = n*10*W and bar = the largest h(lineup.ros_floor[p]) over its pos list. Walk the candidates in order; for each whose pos is in the pos list, with left > 0 and h(ros_pg) > bar: take = min(left, need), add h(ros_pg)*take to the total, subtract take from his left and from need; stop when need is 0. Then add bar*need. ros(roster) is that total, in thousandths of a point: a starter's missed games and byes go to the next candidates who can fill the slot, then to the wire. gain = r(ros(R3) - ros(R1)), where R1 is the owner's values list and R3 is R1 minus send, plus get (get players taken from the partner's values list, matched by name, with their own fields), minus drop. Players in ir_moves stay in R3: they return later, and their games already leave out what they miss. r(d) = ((abs(d) + 50) // 100) / 10 with d's sign: points to one decimal, rounded half away from zero. their.gain = r(ros(H3) - ros(H1)) for the partner: H1 his values list, H3 = H1 minus get, plus send (from the owner's list), minus their.drop. An offer is written only when ros(R3) - ros(R1) >= rules.min_gain*1000 and the partner test of rules.partner holds (rules.min_gain is rules.min_gain_week x weeks_left, one decimal, unless a run sets it). starters(roster), which rules.drop reads: the roster's players with ir false in the candidate order; for each position P of lineup.slots the first n unused of position P, then for each entry of lineup.flex in order the first n unused whose pos is in its list. Lenses (rules.lenses): the same ros(roster) once per lens, in thousandths, with W per lens: the league's windows[lens] for now, push and playoffs, weeks_left for ros; for now, push and playoffs a player's now_games, push_games or po_games in place of games wherever games is read (left and the candidate order too), a null field is 0 games. A lens is blank, its gain and their null, when its W is 0 or when every player of R1, R3, H1 or H3 has a null field. lenses[lens].gain = r(that lens's ros(R3) - ros(R1)) and .their = r(ros(H3) - ros(H1)); the ros lens is gain and their.gain. score = r2(sum over the four lenses of w x my gain in thousandths), w = round(100 x the owner's tier weight for that lens) from rules.standing.weights (ros alone, w 100, when standing has no row for him), a blank lens counting 0, r2(d) = ((abs(d) + 5000) // 10000) / 10 with d's sign. lens.me = the lens with the largest positive w x my gain (ties to the first of now, push, playoffs, ros), null when none; lens.them is the same for the partner with his tier and his gains.
rules.drop: R2 = the owner's values list minus send plus get (get players from the partner's values list, matched by name, each with its own ir_ok, keep and protect, and ir false: a traded player arrives on the bench, never in an IR slot, since 2026-10-29). irs = the players of R2 with ir true. count = the players of R2 with ir false, plus other[owner]. over = count - lineup.cap. When over <= 0, ir_moves and drop are []. Otherwise: (1) IR first. free = max(lineup.ir - irs, 0). Candidates are the players of R2 with ir false and ir_ok true, get players included, ordered by keep descending, then seen descending (as published, 1 decimal), then name ascending. ir_moves = the first min(free, over) candidates, in that order; from here a moved player counts as ir true: he no longer counts toward the cap. over = over - len(ir_moves). (2) Drops. When over > 0: L = the players of R2 with ir false that are not in ir_moves. stay = starters(L) (rules.scoring) plus the get players. pool = the players of L not in stay and with protect false, ordered by keep ascending, then seen ascending (1 decimal), then name ascending. drop = the first `over` of the pool, in that order. When the pool holds fewer than `over` players the offer is not written. keep is the player's rest-of-season points (values.keep = ros_pg x games). Players with protect true are never released (protect is in values: an early draft pick, a player whose keep would start for at least half the other teams at his position, or a player with priced false; never a player ruled out for the season, ros_value season_out, METHODOLOGY 12.111, whose games and keep are 0). K and D/ST (other) are never released or moved. drop and ir_moves are the owner's room; their is the same rule applied to the partner (rules.perceived).
rules.partner: An offer is written only when (1) the partner gains on at least one lens (some lenses[lens].their above 0, rules.lenses), (2) his own tier-weighted lens score is above 0: the whole-percent weights of his tier (rules.standing.weights; ROS alone when the league does not place him) times his lens gains (lenses[lens].their, one decimal, ros being their.gain: his roster after the trade, minus get, plus send, minus his own drop), summed, so a loss of ROS is accepted only when the lenses his tier cares about pay for it, and (3) his perceived gain (rules.perceived) is above rules.min_perc, so he would see it as a gain. David 2026-10-07 for (1), 2026-10-08 for (2) (30a; it replaced a ROS floor with a chaser exemption, which let a chaser give a ROS top-12 player for 0.6 points of short-term gain). Untested heuristic, not backtested: no trade history to test it on.
rules.select: Each owner's list is one ranked list of offers with every partner. It holds, deduplicated by partner, send names and get names: (1) for each position P of QB, RB, WR and TE, the best rules.per_pos (5) offers whose get holds a player at P, at most rules.per_partner_pos (2) of them with one partner; (2) for each partner, the best rules.top (3) offers with that partner. Best = score descending (the owner's lens score, rules.scoring; his ROS gain with no standing), then fewer players (send plus get), then partner name ascending; the list is in that order. With one partner, each set of players asked for appears in at most one offer. An owner with no offer is left out. No offer sends or asks for a player with priced false.
rules.floor: lineup.ros_floor[pos] is the best ros_pg among the league's free-agent file rows that are healthy, on no roster in that league's roster file and not Out or IR, waiver players included (a claim clears in a day or two; a free agent with no rest-of-season row counts 0); 0 when none is left. lineup.floor[pos] is the best proj among the same free agents minus those on waivers (ESPN's waiver flag, the Yahoo leagues' status=W list): next week's wire, for the page's weekly chips, not the gain.
rules.perceived: Untested heuristic (2026-10-05), not backtested: what the partner thinks a player is worth. perceived = seen + 0.5 x streak + leash, 0 for a player whose proj is 0 (out next week) or who is ruled out for the season (ros_value season_out, METHODOLOGY 12.111, since 2026-10-07). streak = last2 - seen (0 with fewer than 2 games), last2 = his average over the last 2 games he played in the league's scoring. leash = 0.5 x max(0, round median - seen) for draft rounds 1-3 only; round median = the median seen of that league's rostered players drafted in that round who have played. The round is the league's draft file's; a player that league never drafted has none, and ESPN's round for the same player stands in only for a league with no draft file at all. The partner's perceived gain = his weekly lineup by perceived after the trade minus before (players with ir false, fixed slots then flex, highest perceived first), every slot floored at the best available free agent by perceived, his roster after the trade minus their.ir_moves and their.drop. their = rules.drop applied to the partner: R2 = the partner's values list minus get plus send (send players from the owner's values list, each with its own fields), other[partner], and his incoming players (send) never dropped; an offer whose partner has no legal drop is not written. How the perceived gain decides whether an offer is written: rules.partner. Not in values: a reader cannot re-derive perceived.
rules.namesake: No offer's get holds a player the partner's team name is built on: a player whose first or last name (letters and apostrophes, 4+ characters, not Jr or Sr) appears inside the partner's team name, case-blind.
rules.chips: chips per player: "Hot" when streak >= 4.0, "Cold" when streak <= -4.0 (streak = last2 - seen, unrounded), "Early pick" for a draft round 1-3 (the league's draft file; ESPN's round for the same player only in a league with no draft file). last2 is null with fewer than 2 games.
rules.lenses: Four lenses price the same lineup over four windows of weeks (David 2026-10-07): now = the next 2 weeks, push = the next 4, this week counted, playoffs = the fantasy playoff weeks still to play, ros = the rest of the season. The league's windows holds the weeks still to play in each; a player's games in a window are now_games, push_games and po_games in values (ros: games), byes out. Every lens prices a player at his ros_pg, so lenses differ only in which games count: points in a window, never a new price (METHODOLOGY 12.109: a playoff schedule factor failed). They only re-sort (score, rules.scoring) and filter (rules.partner) offers, from an untested heuristic. Not backtested; the weights are judgment (rules.standing).

standing.tiers: Tier by games back of the last playoff seed, where games back is half the gap in wins minus losses (David 2026-10-07), counted in weeks: ESPN's is halved again because it pays a bonus win each week (David 2026-10-08). 1 or more games clear is a contender, less than 1 clear to less than 2 behind is a bubble team, 2 or more behind is a chaser. A judgment, not backtested.
standing.blend: Each tier weighs the four lenses (now, push, playoffs, ROS) as a blend that keeps a ROS share in every tier (David 2026-10-07). Lenses are points in a window at the ROS rate; they re-sort and filter offers and never change a price. Not backtested.

rules.notes: notes lists the bye facts of an offer, as data without words: Team Watch writes the copy by kind. Each note is {kind, side, player, week, n}; side is me (the owner) or them (the partner) and player an incoming player of that side. covers_bye: he plays the earliest week a kept player at his position (on that side's roster, not sent) is on bye and he is not; week is that week and n the kept players at his position on bye then. bye_done: his bye is over while a player his side sends has one ahead; week is the earliest of those byes and n the sent players with a bye ahead. A player without byes_left makes no note.
